Also resolve open findings 6HAHVX and VDYV5B by these fixes. Read first: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/closure-2026-11-26/DECISIONS.md (owner decisions, binding), /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/closure-2026-11-26/claude-execution-handoff.txt (your workstream section, 'Combined acceptance cases', 'Final evidence and stop condition'), the matching lane directory in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/closure-2026-11-26 and full-report.txt for Codex's reproductions. Rules: start with FAILING tests built from Codex's reproductions (show each fails before the fix), then the fix at the boundary named, then sweep siblings. Do not touch init's README ordering or merge other PRs (the integrator does that). Full gate by exit code: just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test (pty and network unsandboxed), just fuzz-check if callisto-model public signatures change, just bench if git processes are involved. Then git fetch origin main && codex review --base origin/main; fix every actionable finding inside your boundary, re-gate, repeat until nothing actionable; a finding that contradicts DECISIONS.md is reported, not acted on. Commit locally (signed). Report: final sha, each failing-first test and its oracle, each codex round, gate exit codes. Do NOT push, resolve findings, or open PRs. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be thorough before a push: a push costs a paid review, so find problems locally first.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Before reporting a change as ready to push, run the AGENTS.md gate in full and judge each by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test` (workspace-wide, not just the touched crate; tests elsewhere read scripts, specs and error registries). Run network/pty tests unsandboxed. Iterate with scoped `cargo test -p` while working.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Every push triggers a paid review. Before reporting, run the checklist in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/d58474bb/tmp/review-checklist.md against your full diff. Push once, only after the lead has read your diff and says push; for an existing PR, commit locally and report the worktree and sha first.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.
- Findings: the lead writes a row in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/FINDINGS-LEDGER.md (class, owning boundary, codebase-wide sweep, fix level) before any fix is briefed. If you find a finding without a row, stop and ask the lead.
- Prompt UI is final: line-based lists (plain text + inquire single-line Text). Findings about the prompt library's own behaviour are dismissed with a documented limit; fix only behaviour Callisto owns. Never redesign the prompt UI in response to a finding.

Do not add a submodule override:the native annotated-tag/on-demand lead was refuted. Explicitrefspec already overridesremote.push/push.default.

Add one narrowly named best-effort stderr presentation operation in output.rs (or an equivalent existing sink). It accepts a supplied writer where tests need injection, attempts the formatted write, and returns no error that can replace the command result. Use it for advisory/diagnostic echoes and final error rendering, including the runner's redacted live echo. Continue capturing/draining the child after a failed echo. Make PendingWork's advisory emission non-failing in its API and migrate every call site, including init. Make the whole release-preview note emitter best effort, because its other lines are advisory too. For init, required interactive narration/review remains distinct from an optional pending-work note. A blanket drop(Notes.emit(...)) everywhere is not an adequate design: decide emission policy at the note boundary while retaining report data and exactly-once normal-output behavior. Existing init wrapper already preserves the primary error on its failure path by discarding only a late note emission failure. Preserve that ownership.

Do not swallow errors from file writes, receipt/intent commits, child execution/capture failures, or required interactive prompts. Do not globally convert CliError::Io into success. - `completions <shell>` and `schema` exit 0 without printing an error or panicking when stdout's reading end is already closed (e.g. piped into a command that exits early); a `--format json` report command's write error in that same situation propagates as `E213` and exits 1.

- A changeset naming an unknown or ambiguous package produces an error-level diagnostic naming the changeset file, so `status --check` exits 1; one naming a package in the colon form (`cargo:lib`) fails `status` with E316 and exit 1, with or without `--check`; a changeset with no entries at all is an info-level diagnostic and never fails 
- hangeset that fails to parse (blank summary with entries, malformed entry, missing or unclosed frontmatter) produces an error-level diagnostic naming the file and the parse error, so `status --check` exits 1.
- `status --strict` reports strict-escalatable warnings as errors, so `status --check --strict` exits 1 where `status --check` exits 0.

---
callisto-cli: minor
---

**`init` and `release --dry-run` say less and say what to do next**

`init` prints each note once and a one-line summary of the generated workflow instead of its whole text, and `release --dry-run` now points the way when it cannot show what you expect.

- `init` prints each note once on stderr, with `--format json` too, where the report also lists them; in an interactive run the notes come before the write question and a decline keeps them.
- `init` names the workflow file, the branch it runs on and what it does, instead of printing the file.
- `init --workflow` in an already configured workspace says it wrote the workflow instead of claiming it initialized the configuration.
- `release --dry-run` says to run `callisto version` (or merge the release PR) first while it has work for the packages being released; `release` says it too when there is nothing to release yet or the selection is not a release.
  - With `--package`, only work for the selected packages and their groups counts.
  - In a prerelease cycle, notes `callisto version` already applied do not count.
  - It reads changesets only, so it works in a shallow clone too.
  - When a release is planned, `release --dry-run --format json` also lists it in the report's `diagnostics`; with nothing to release the note is on stderr only.
  - If the check cannot run, one note names the error code; run `callisto status` for the cause.
- An `origin` that is not a hosted remote, such as a local path or a `file://` URL, previews like no `origin`: the dry run shows the plan with one note that says why tags are unbound.
  - A real `callisto release` refuses it with an error that names the accepted forms: an `https://` or `ssh://git@` URL, or `git@host:owner/repo`.
  - The error never shows the `origin` value; run `git remote get-url --push origin` to see it.
- `init` accepts a non-hosted `origin` the same way, since it never pushes, and says once that it is not hosted.
.changeset/tough-pandas-leap.md

content.content:
Pre-push self-review checklist (from recurring Entire reviewer findings). Check your full diff against every item; fix or justify each before reporting. Every push triggers a paid review: do not push until the lead says so.

1. Secrets: no user-supplied URL, remote, token, env value or path that may carry credentials is printed in any message, error, JSON or log. Print only values we derived ourselves (owner/repo slug, package names). Child processes get the runner's filtered environment.
2. Same structure for preview and real: dry runs, hints and previews compute on exactly the set/plan the real command uses (selection, group expansion, publishable packages, roster). No second derivation.
3. Modes: text vs --format json vs non-TTY. JSON stdout stays a single document; human notes go to stderr once in both modes; json never prompts. Check every new message in all three modes.
4. Validation order: mode/eligibility first, then input validation, then prompts or side effects. A bad input never reaches a confirmation screen.
5. Optional conveniences (preselection, detection, previews, hints) degrade with a warning; they never make the command fail.
6. Never parse text we rendered, and never hand-parse a foreign grammar (Markdown, git URLs, shell) beyond the coarse classification we need; prefer the owning tool or omit.
7. Rust: exhaustive match on our own enums (no _ arm); no unwrap outside tests; expect names its invariant; no swallowed errors (.ok(), drop(result)) without a one-line reason; no process::exit outside main; Drop-based cleanup; no global mutable state unless unavoidable; minimal visibility.
8. Edge inputs for anything touching user paths or strings: spaces, newlines, leading ':' or '-', unicode, empty, very long.
9. Tests: one test per behaviour through the real binary where users see it; tests clean up children and temp files on failure.
11. Consumers: for every function, field, type or enum variant whose behaviour or meaning you changed, list every reader (rg the name across crates, including the changelog, version planner, release preview, PR body, JSON reports and tests) and confirm each still gets what it expects. A value with two jobs must be split, not repurposed.
10. Precedent: when a behaviour has a well-known precedent (git, cargo, npm, changesets), follow it and cite it rather than inventing.

fix(cli): a closed stdout or stderr never changes a command's result

Advisory stderr (notes, warnings, a child's echoed output, the error card) goes through one best-effort `advise`, so a failed write can no longer replace E169, turn exit 2 into a 101 panic, or stop the runner draining a child. Every command writes stdout through one sink that treats a closed pipe as the end of output. Required prompts, reports and file writes stay fallible. Clippy's print lints and a disallowed `std::io::stdout` replace the source-scanning println test.

The process-count oracle now compares auto against changeset packages with tags at an older version, under the modern and a pre-2.44 tag listing, with a positive control that the legacy listing leaves tags of tags to a lookup. The aggregate tests build their tag index from that legacy listing, prove the cache miss, and add an active positive control; disabled inference no longer checks for full history.

#!/bin/sh
# Counts git processes for dual cargo/npm packages in a v2 pre cycle keyed by npm names.
set -e
BIN=$1
for n in 2 6; do
  D=/tmp/claude-501/w2-pre-$n
  rm -rf "$D"; mkdir -p "$D"; cd "$D"
  git init -q -b main; git config user.email t@e; git config user.name t; git config commit.gpgsign false
  members=""; keys=""; ws=""
  i=0
  while [ $i -lt $n ]; do
    mkdir -p d$i/src
    printf '[package]\nname = "d%s-rs"\nversion = "1.0.0"\nedition = "2021"\ndescription = "d"\nlicense = "MIT"\n' $i > d$i/Cargo.toml
    touch d$i/src/lib.rs
    printf '{"name":"d%s-js","version":"1.0.0"}\n' $i > d$i/package.json
    members="$members\"d$i\","; ws="$ws\"d$i\","; keys="$keys\"d$i-js\":\"1.0.0\","
    i=$((i+1))
  done
  printf '[workspace]\nmembers = [%s]\nresolver = "2"\n' "${members%,}" > Cargo.toml
  printf '{"name":"root","private":true,"workspaces":[%s]}\n' "${ws%,}" > package.json
  printf '# pre\n' > callisto.toml
  mkdir -p .changeset
  printf '{"mode":"pre","tag":"alpha","initialVersions":{%s},"changesets":[]}\n' "${keys%,}" > .changeset/pre.json
  git add -A; git commit -qm "enter pre"
  for args in "--dry-run release" "--dry-run version"; do
    rm -f trace.json
    GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=$D/trace.json "$BIN" $args > /dev/null 2> err.txt || { echo "n=$n $args failed"; cat err.txt; }
    echo "n=$n $args: $(grep -c '"event":"start"' trace.json)"
  done
done

Piping into a command that stops reading early (`callisto status | head`) or running with stderr closed now leaves the exit status as it would be otherwise.

- Every command, in text and JSON alike, treats a closed stdout as the end of its output instead of failing with E213.
- Notes, warnings, a publishing tool's echoed output and the final error card are best effort: a closed stderr no longer crashes `callisto` with exit 101, a usage error still exits 2, and a refused release keeps its own error code.
- A file `callisto` must write, such as a changeset or a receipt, still fails the command when it cannot be written.

fix(release): batch pre.json history reads, retryable init, help through the stdout sink

`pre.json` keys a package's first manifest did not name where `pre.json` was added (a moved manifest, or another ecosystem's name of a dual package) are searched for together: the first miss at that commit runs one `git grep` for every key and reads its matches in one batch, so the pending-version hint no longer adds git processes per package to `release --dry-run`. `files_containing_at` takes several needles.

`init` writes `.changeset/README.md` before `callisto.toml`, so a README it cannot write leaves no config and a plain retry completes. `callisto help` renders through the shared stdout sink, so a closed stdout no longer fails it with E213. The spec and changeset now promise best effort only for notes, warnings, echoed output and the error card; output a command needs on stderr stays fallible.
